Subject: Request: temporary transfer exception + TIA scoping for pilot

Hi Mina,

Quick context — SolaraHealth is starting a 3-month pilot with our analytics partner (CloudEdge Consulting) to run de-id and enrichment on a subset of records. For operational reasons the partner will process data in the US region; our procurement and legal teams need confirmation that Redwood can support a limited routing exception for the pilot and what evidence you can provide.

Two immediate asks from our side:
- Can Redwood provide a scoped TIA (or DTIA) that covers this specific pilot (only analytic outputs, not raw patient texts)? We need a list of the safeguards you will assert.
- CloudEdge will act as an approved subprocessor for the pilot. Can Redwood certify their subprocessors (they subcontract some ETL) or provide a certification path checklist we can rely on?

I attached a one-page dataflow diagram and the pilot statement of work. Also copied procurement (procurement@solarahealth.com) and Anya (CloudEdge) who is leading the integration.

Thanks,
Tom Sullivan

SolaraHealth

Hi all — putting forward a practical mutual action plan and a first-pass TIA scope. See attached draft TIA and short timeline. Key points up-front:
- Scope: only transformed analytic outputs (no raw patient text transfer to CloudEdge).
- Duration: pilot window (2026-07-05 — 2026-09-30) with automatic revocation of routing exception afterwards unless a separate contract is agreed.
- Subprocessor certification: we can provide a checkpointed checklist + evidence package for CloudEdge (SOC2 Type II summary, subprocessors list, signed subprocessor attestations).
- Controls we will assert in the TIA: prefix/KV caching bounded to region, strict KV ACL for processors, per-request logging retained for 90 days for the pilot, and signed data use limitations in DPA addendum.

Deliverables & dates: 
- 2026-06-30: Redwood provides draft TIA + checklist (attached).
- 2026-07-02: CloudEdge returns subprocessor CSV and SOC snapshot.
- 2026-07-06: Joint evidence review call; finalize routing exception.

Tom / Procurement — if that timeline works we'll send the TIA-draft link now: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bExampleDriveLink (TIA: tia-draft-solarahealth-v1.docx).

Subject: Re: Request: temporary transfer exception + TIA scoping for pilot

Tom / team — legal note:
- Baseline documents: SCCs (EU), UK IDTA + UK Addendum (if Solara has UK subjects) remain the contract anchors. Any routing exception must be tightly scopped in the DPA addendum and time-boxed.
- Subprocessor certification: Redwood cannot "certify" third-party subcontractors on behalf of customers, but we can: 1) require CloudEdge to provide a signed subprocessors CSV, 2) collect SOC2 summary and 3) obtain subprocessors' written attestation of limited access (we can accept reasonable redactions).
- Additional ask: we will require a documented data minimization statement from CloudEdge and a signed attestation that any subcontractor access is ephemeral and logged.

If UK data subjects are in scope, we will also require the UK IDTA addendum to be executed and evidence that CloudEdge will honor the Addendum obligations (we can include a flow-down clause in our addendum). For the pilot we can accept a conditional flow (exception) provided the evidence packages are delivered before the July 6 review call.

Redlines: we'll prepare a short DPA addendum template with a 90-day routing exception clause + rollback triggers (security incident, unauthorized subprocessor use). Expect a first redline by EOD 2026-07-01.

—Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
